title: Llama 3.1 405B (Meta) — open frontier giant
hardware: Multi-GPU server or ~240GB RAM at 4-bit; most users use hosted endpoints
best_for: Research at the open frontier and distilling smaller models.
description: The first openly available model to match closed frontier models: 405 billion dense parameters under the Llama Community License, free for most commercial use. It proved open weights could play at the top tier and became the standard teacher for distilling smaller open models. Few run it locally — it is usually reached through hosted providers — but its existence reset what 'open' means.

demo.code:
# Usually via a hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint:
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI(base_url="https://api.provider.example/v1", api_key="KEY")
r = client.chat.completions.create(model="meta-llama/Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Why do open weights matter?"}])
print(r.choices[0].message.content)

provenance: Public model cards, provider documentation, and open model repository metadata.

title: Llama 3.3 70B (Meta) — the open sweet spot
hardware: ~40GB VRAM at 4-bit (single high-end GPU or dual mid GPUs)
best_for: Self-hosted chatbots, private RAG, fine-tuning bases.
description: Llama 3.3 70B matched the previous 405B flagship's quality at a fraction of the size — the sweet spot of the open world. Multilingual, 128K context, and the most fine-tuned open model family in existence, it is the default answer to 'which open model should I self-host.'

demo.code:
from transformers import pipeline
pipe = pipeline("text-generation", model="meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct", device_map="auto")
print(pipe("Explain open source in one sentence.", max_new_tokens=60)[0]["generated_text"])
# gated repo: request access, then huggingface-cli login

best_for: Open reasoning on a single GPU with thinking mode.

title: Qwen2.5-Coder 32B (Alibaba) — open code champion
best_for: Self-hosted code completion and repo-aware assistance.
description: The open code model that beat much bigger rivals on coding benchmarks: trained on 5.5 trillion tokens of code, 92 languages, 128K context, Apache 2.0. The default self-hosted copilot brain.

demo.code:
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct")
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct", device_map="auto")
ids = tok("def fibonacci(n):", return_tensors="pt").input_ids
print(tok.decode(model.generate(ids, max_new_tokens=100)[0]))
